utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but in the Serbian original it says: "I did not want" -- oh, I see here that those two are joined -- no, they're not joined. 35 paragraph states that: "I left my house and went towards the centre of the village to see what was happening."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, you were not escaping but you went to the village to see what was going on because you understood that they were not chasing you and that they could have killed you had they wanted to?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what it says in paragraph 35 is not correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: It's not correct the way you put it in your question. You skipped the paragraph where it says that there was shooting -- they were shooting after me so I escaped to the centre of the village to escape the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that paragraph, when they fired at you, was not that one. You said immediately after paragraph 35 it says that's where they found you at the door and they did not shoot at you. And then in paragraph 35, before there was any shooting at you, you said that you saw a man who was lying down and then you understood his sign to mean that they should go on - I don't want to mention any names. And then you said: "I left my house to the centre of the village -- towards the centre of the village to see what was happening. The shooting was still going on and there was a lot of confusion." Is this correct what you say or not?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: It is not correct because I came to Murat's house and then I said what happened after that. I was not going to the centre of the village, I didn't manage to reach it.

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: He was shooting after me. I don't know why he didn't hit me.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Um, Your Honours, I wonder if we should have a redaction at lines 17 to 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1004072 [as interpreted], please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you give the number again, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D04072.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It seems that Mr. Robinson's advice didn't work.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In what way, if you can please tell me. I'm trying to check the assertions of this witness and I'm more concerned about the statements that become evidence rather than documents, which I will easily check through other witnesses. What I'm concerned about is the attention the Trial Chamber will pay to generalised statements by witnesses and I -- actually, I can only go through this statement with this witness, with nobody else. I was given advice, but my sense of danger from those statements is such that I feel that I have to contest those statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, I won't repeat what I said earlier on, but this is -- this seems to be a statement given by a third person, and what I told you yesterday to you was to have a word with Mr. Robinson whether or not you should put a statement of a third person to the current witness. And if yes, how to put it. Please proceed. You have five minutes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you hear that -- or rather, do you see this statement of Mr. Selimovic and these names that he mentions as an illegally armed group?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: It is barely legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Fadil, son of Ibis from Zaklopaca; Hamidovic Huso who you mention from Zaklopaca; then Mustafa Avdic from Zaklopaca; then Avdic Selim from Zaklopaca, all of these names --

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: There is no Selim Avdic in Zaklopaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Amir Selimovic. It's more legible in English.

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Salihovic, I guess, not Selimovic from Zaklopaca and then this one from Milici and so on. Are you saying that you did not know that this group was armed with weapons that are not personal weapons but military ones?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: I repeat that I did not know of any group that had weapons and I do not know of any statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But, Mr. Hodzic, if somebody is chasing after Huso and Huso is armed and this somebody knows that Huso is armed, then you should say that you do not know the reason why he is being chased?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: This is the first time that I hear of Huso being chased. There are two Husos. Who do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hodzic. Now, this description, how the attack started, that is page 7 in Serbian and 5 and 6 in English, your statement. You say that many cars passed by and in one case you say that you were in the house shaving and in this other case you said something different, in the interview you said something different. How do you explain these discrepancies, differences?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: I explained them because one statement is abbreviated and the other one is given at greater length because that's what I was asked to do. Locations -- I was asked to say exactly where I was at every point in time. That is why the statements differ. One is shorter and the other one is more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 7 in this statement and on page 6 probably in English you say that you were confused and you remember that your mother told me in a hurried way to go because she was afraid for you. You opened the door and you saw two men in camouflage uniforms. On their sleeves they had red ribbons. Why did your mother think that you were in danger rather than her? Was it because you had deserted or because you were a participant in some agreements about organising a unit?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Um, could I just ask which statement we're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 22529, Serb page 7, English page 5 and then 6. This paragraph is probably on page 6.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: My mother feared for her own safety too because she grabbed her daughter-in-law, who was preparing some food at the time, and as she was running through the hallway with her she knocked at my door and said, "Run, what are you waiting for? There is shooting going on." Go and check this. I did not organise anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellencies. If I don't have any more time, I'm not going to call up any more documents. Then I'm going to do it with somebody else. Thank you, Mr. Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, briefly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I can just have your indulgence for a moment, Your Honours, to find the page reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, Dr. Karadzic said to you on page 49, lines 23 and 24, he said: "And then you saw that some people had been shot from hunting rifles, is that correct, or with hunting ammunition?" Do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, having just reviewed yesterday your statement as we talked about earlier today, do you recall ever having said that some people had been shot from hunting rifles or with hunting ammunition?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: I think that I mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And when you mentioned that, who were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If you mentioned people who had been shot with hunting rifles or with -- using hunting ammunition, were you referring to the large group of victims you thought -- you saw through the village or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: Five persons I saw with my own eyes: Rifet Hodzic, Bajro Salihovic, Salko Salihovic, Becir Hodzic, and Bajro Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies that. Now, in paragraph or at page 51 Dr. Karadzic asked you the question: "In paragraph 37 you say that you were listening to the radio and how Fadil Turkovic, the commander of the Muslim Green Berets, had come to Zaklopaca and killed 65 villagers in retaliation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, was it not para 57? I think he clarified later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Perhaps so, and then it would be my mistake, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you remember Dr. Karadzic referring you to paragraph 57 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to upload so that the witness can follow what --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Wonderful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And Dr. Karadzic said -- oh, I see, Your Honours. This is paragraph 57. "Did you not hear that Fadil Turkovic came to a Serb village and killed the inhabitants." And you said: "No, this is quite the opposite and I have witnesses who were there. We all heard on the transistor radio announced that Fadil Turkovic on such and such a day at such and such a time killed Muslims in such and such a village because they did not want to join the Green Berets." To your knowledge was that radio report true in any regard?

utterances.speaker: SEAD HODZIC
utterances.text: That is impossible. For heaven's sake, why would a man come and kill his own men? Fadil was not Mitar Simic's commander and the commander of the other Serbs. Mr. Karadzic is saying that he was commander of the Green Berets and there were no Serbs among the Green Berets. Why would Fadil come and kill Muslims, his own people. It is the Serbs who did that and not Fadil. This is a pure lie.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't have any other questions in re-direct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bazdar, now your evidence has come to an end --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, but that's Mr. Hodzic, not Mr. Bazdar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. My apologies, Mr. Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We've had a busy day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we have. Mr. Hodzic, your evidence has been concluded. On behalf of my colleagues and the Tribunal as a whole, I thank you for coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you for your time, for listening to me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And have a pleasant trip back to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- home.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I just noticed in the transcript today at page 50, lines 4 to 7 --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: -- I think actually that that might call for a redaction as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this statement, 1D4073.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be taken care of.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That proposal for decoration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't have the English translation for that, but I suppose the Prosecution would not oppose to marking it for identification?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If I could just have your indulgence for a second to see, again, quickly which document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The proposition for decoration of Mustafa ...

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Oh, no. I actually do object, Your Honour. The witness did not confirm any part of that document in any regard, knew absolutely nothing of it, and I think it hasn't passed any bench-mark. The document, furthermore, doesn't appear to be an original document and, frankly, I noticed further it's not related to the admissibility of the document, Dr. Karadzic didn't read out all of the passage that was even marked to the witness. But I do object to the admission of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But did the witness not deny the -- deny the involvement in arming or whatever of that person in question, who was proposed to be decorated? So in terms -- whether -- my question is: It is contextually relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I need to check the transcript, Your Honour. I think he did not claim knowledge of it rather than specifically deny it, which is, in my submission, a difference. If I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think I see your point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson or Mr. Karadzic, would you like to reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think that your approach is correct, that if we can only admit documents that a witness agrees with then we're creating a skewed form of admissibility and when a document is contradictory to the witness and he explains it then it ought to be admitted for its context and I think that's the case here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Would you like to add, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just to keep our eye on the ball of what I think have been an evolving set of guide-lines. Of course there's no dispute that where a document is used for appropriate contextual reasons or to impeach a witness, that it's not necessary for the witness to affirm its contents. But that leaves aside the -- or begs the question of the underlying indicia of authenticity about the document as used. Otherwise any document could be presented to a witness who would in the guise of impeachment. So I understood there are basically two factors governing the admissibility of documents used for impeachment or context. And one is of course whether that is its purpose; and number two, other indicia of reliability or authenticity. No question in instances where we've had contemporaneous documents produced by various official entities. And then I -- there's a bit of a sliding scale thereafter. So I think the issue under discussion here is: Where does this document come from? To what extent can it be relied on for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for my memory. The witness did confirm that he knew that person in question, did he not?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I have what I see right now is the witness repeating that he does not know of any group that had weapons --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, that person --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: -- and he did not know of any statements. And as for the person ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With the first name of Mustafa, if my memory is correct -- I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may add something, this is an original Telex of the committee commemorating the anniversary of Srebrenica. There's a date, there's a number and there's a reference to the body that made the proposal. You cannot place a stamp on a Telex. And the Army of Republika Srpska seized this in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When the other party is challenging the authenticity and in -- in particular in the case where the witness did not confirm content of any part of the document, you need to call a witness who can introduce that document in a proper way. Your questions remain an -- and answer of the witness will remain in the transcript and the document later admitted can be used to assess the credibility of the witness. In that regards we will not admit this document through this witness. Thank you, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can I rise on one further almost by now administrative thing. I had asked for paragraph 37 to be redacted, I see also paragraph 39 will need to be of the 92 ter written evidence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In its entirety?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I think that's safer, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. That will be done. Very well, for -- shall we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the time, the Chamber will take a break for an hour and resume at 25 past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.23 p.m.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the witness takes the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, I once again would like to inform you on behalf of the Chamber that you will be testifying today with the benefit of pseudonym, which is KDZ-607, image and voice distortion. This means that there will be no reference to your real name or information which might reveal your identity to the public or media. The audio/visual record of your testimony which is broadcast to the public will have a distorted image which can be shown at the monitor right now, like this, to ensure that your identity is protected and the transcript, while available to the public, will always refer to your pseudonym. Do you understand, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have 65 ter number 90274 called up, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, on the computer monitor in front of you within a couple of seconds you're going to see a sheet of paper. And when you see it, I would like you to tell us whether or not your name appears there correctly. All right. Just hang on for a couple of moments. Do you see your name now, Mr. Witness, on the computer screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we have that pseudonym sheet marked as our first Prosecution exhibit in relation to this witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Of course under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit P3288 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Witness, you have given statements to authorities or offices from your own country as well as to representatives from the Office of the Prosecutor for this Tribunal; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you've also testified in another court about what happened to you in 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, on the 1st of September, last week, you met with more representatives from the Office of the Prosecutor and they read back to you another statement. And that statement put together parts of your evidence from your earlier statements and transcripts so that it's organised in a chronological way; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And at that time you made some corrections and you added some information and you clarified some information in that statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you signed it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And with those changes, is that statement you signed last week accurate as far as you remember the events it talks about?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And if today I was to ask you all the same questions you were asked when you gave your earlier statements and you testified in other trials, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Then, Your Honours, could we have the amalgamated statement of this witness, 65 ter 90272, as the next Prosecution exhibit under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3289 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, because of the nature of the evidence in regard to this witness, I don't intend on reading a summary and will move directly to some questions related to the written evidence we've just admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, when you listened to your statement on the 1st of September being read back to you and also when we met this last weekend to prepare for you to come here today, you looked at a number of documents. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I just want to talk about some of these documents briefly with you. In your written evidence at paragraph 15, you refer to a photo of Rasadnik farm and make a comment on it, and that was a black-and-white photo. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Ms. Edgerton. My apology for intervention, but shall we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we have a look at 19145E, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, is that a colour version of the photograph you commented on in your written statement at paragraph 15?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this is simply offered up now rather than the black-and-white photograph so that we can have a clearer depiction of the image. So I'd like to tender that as a Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3290, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: At paragraph 54 of your written evidence you referred to a lengthy document which was a series of exhumation records relating to remains exhumed from a mass grave site. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we see, please, 65 ter number 09394 without broadcasting it, and starting at page 2 of the document in both English and B/C/S move slowly through the first few pages. If we could go to the next page, please, in B/C/S. And the next page. And one page following in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, looking at the first few pages of this document, can you say whether this is the same document you reviewed and commented on in your statement?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: As you reviewed this document, did you have a look at the names of those people whose remains were identified?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did those names correspond with the list of persons you identified as victims in paragraph 48 and 49 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we have that, please, as the next Prosecution exhibit, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure of the status of this document be admitted it as P3276, only part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Only two pages of it, Your Honour, so now I would like to move the whole file, the witness having reviewed the whole file.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think the first eight pages should be admitted, but the other document -- this is a 69-page document. Beyond the names there's no real connection between that other information and this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any response?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Um, the certificates that the witness reviewed establish the death of the persons killed in this case, Your Honours, and I would say they're relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it you don't dispute the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view there's a basis to admit the document in its entirety. That will be done -- or added -- that will be added to the existing document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be done, that will be added to the existing exhibit, but shall I go -- shall we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we go now to 65 ter number 07047.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, this document is dated 14 June 2004 and it's an official record prepared by the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska regarding collection centres in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And if we could go into private session for this question, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, if we could go over to the second page in the original document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you see those two names we've just spoken about on the list in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: One question about this document that I think I should ask in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we go back to page 1 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Witness, could you tell us if you see the name of the individual we've just spoken about on this list?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like to try and tender this document, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As well as the previous one?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, no objection as to this document. As to the previous one, Mr. President, if you look at the text, I think that what the witness had to say about this document is so limited compared to what the conclusions that the text draws that it would be unfair to admit this document. This was a document that was created in 2004 and it's some kind of investigation that was done or conclusions that were made well after these events, more than ten years after the events, as to who was responsible for various facilities. And these are issues that we think that this witness doesn't sufficiently speak to the document about to warrant its admission. He can say what he observed at the places where he were, but to use that as a bootstrap to admit someone's conclusions from Republika Srpska about who was in charge of these facilities, we don't think that that's fair, given the fact that we don't have anyone to really confront about the conclusions that are being drawn from -- in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to respond, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness's evidence, admittedly, with respect to this document is limited to identifying the location or identifying the detention facility where he was housed. Establishing that there was or could have been no other place than that facility that the document refers to and I actually think given that evidence it passes the established bench-mark here in these proceedings for document admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All the witness did was to identify the building where he was detained.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: This is a document from the Republika Srpska. I don't know that there is any dispute as to its authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber agrees with the observation of Mr. Robinson and this will not be admitted through this witness, but we'll give the number for 70330.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit Number P3291.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could just go into private session for the first part of the question in relation to the next document, I would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it there's no objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3292, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. And I have no further questions from this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As indicated, the Chamber will have a break for ten minutes. In the meantime I would like to encourage the parties to have a word as to how to proceed in terms of cross-examination, in particular what should be dealt with in private session and what should be -- what can be discussed in public session. We'll resume at 2.30. --- Break taken at 2.19 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Um, Your Honour, I've reviewed the paragraphs that we think could be dealt with in open session and discussed them with Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Robinson, and we will do our best. Dr. Karadzic, we realised, will have some difficulty because he is working with an older version of the amalgamated statement, although this version with the changes was disclosed to him in plenty of time. Sometimes with the best intentions on all our parts, things go awry. And so with your understanding in that regard, we will do our best. And before I sit down I just wanted to because I hadn't before we broke, move the remaining associated exhibits that weren't otherwise dealt with with this witness in oral testimony into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A couple of associated exhibits have been dealt with -- one we deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And there are some that have been already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I draw your attention to the document with 65 ter number 07047, which is referred to in para 56.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that is the one that Your Honours have ruled should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: -- dealt with with another witness. So when I said those that weren't dealt with in oral testimony, I included that because it wasn't dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- I meant to refer to the next one 07330, which is referred to in para 57. If you read para 57, all that the witness said is that: "I haven't been shown this document, payment list."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Um, we dealt with that in live evidence, Your Honours, and Mr. Robinson was asked whether he had any objection to its admission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: -- and he did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That was admitted at 3291. I noted erroneously the number. Thank you. Then the others can be admitted -- actually, 19145A.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted as -- we give the number right now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3293, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And 19145C.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Will be Exhibit P3294.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: -- that covers it, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And after today I will be reviewing the transcript, Your Honours, to see what can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to kindly ask you and be mindful of it myself that we should be making a pause between question and answer in order that the interpreters may interpret what we are saying. Were you aware of the presence of two armies in the area you were?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that there were two armed forces, two armies, present in the area where you lived?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I don't know which two armed forces are you referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that there were armed Serbs in various formations there as well as armed Muslims, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: In my area, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was not present at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P3292 called up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it to appear, Mr. Witness, do you agree that in the direction of Central Bosnia the separation lines between the Muslim and Serbian armies were west of Kaljina, near Sokolac, close to Olovo and Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I'm -- don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to look at the document you were reading, Kozarde, Kramer Selo, et cetera, where it is stated: "A concentrated presence of the enemy forces was noted, probably the intention is to cut off the Srednje-Nisici road, et cetera. So the telegram that was shown a moment ago and admitted into evidence speaks about an increased presence of your forces there. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at without it being broadcast your statement paragraph 38.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 12, please, or rather, paragraph 38, wherever it may be, but I do believe it's on page 12 -- 13, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at what it is you have to say there and I will read it in English. [In English] [As read] "... According to my information, which I learned when I reached the free territory, the defenders of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were attacked at that elevation, they all went up towards the elevation." [Interpretation] And then, speaking about the critical day, I will not mention what the event was, you say that there were also persons wounded and killed; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was this other side that wounded these individuals and killed several Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I don't know about the killing of the Serbs, but I do know that when we were being used as human shield there were people wounded among us. Some people say that three persons were wounded. I know the names of two. I don't know about the third one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what was the army against which you were used as a human shield?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Against the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This means that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was present after all?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes, but you asked me about the Kalinovik area which I wasn't aware of. The first question you put to me had to do with Kalinovik, and that's on the side opposite to the area where we were used as a human shield.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That must have been an error in interpretation because I said "in the area where you lived." So where you lived, in your municipality, the telegram which makes reference to these various villages, does it accurately report about the fact that the enemy forces were observed and of course to the author of the telegram, that would have been the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Well, the villages that I mentioned did not have the presence of the BH army at all. Let me just tell you my village had 57 inhabitants. 22 of them were men, the rest were women. Six of them moved out. I am giving you the information as per the 1991 census. In 1992 six of them had already moved out. Out of the 22 men, four were elderly individuals, 65 and above, and there were five minors. So how can one speak of an army at all in those terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we have any time left, we'll get back to that. In your earlier statements you also speak of the circumstances prevailing in your municipality and say that the Serbs set up their own Assembly and introduced parallel municipal structures. Is it not true that the Serbs and the Muslims, i.e., the SDS and the SDA, agreed that the municipality would be transformed into two municipalities, Serb and Muslim, and that the Serbian Assembly functioned as a Deputies Club or as a part of the National Assembly and that the Executive Committee did not exist at all until the outbreak of hostilities, until May?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: In early 1992, or rather, in late 1991, the Serbian Municipal Assembly was set up headed by Tomislav Batinic, who had up to that point been the legitimate president or president of a legitimate Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, the joint Assembly continued to work; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I know that for a while the Assembly did not work. I think it was from December 1991 until May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that they divided, or rather, agreed to divide the building. Half of it was the Serb municipality, the other half of it was the Muslim municipality, and also the public security station, half to the Serbs and half to the Muslims and they had their separate doors and they even celebrated that with a cocktail party?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I know about the police station, but I don't know about the agreement. The police was divided because the Serbs said that they no longer trusted the Muslims. I'm sorry, let me just go back to this establishment of a Serb municipality. At the time they were justifying it by a lack of balance in the members of the Assembly, in the Municipal Assembly. The Bosniaks won 30 seats and the Serbs 20. So they said that they wanted to have the police divided because they no longer trusted the Muslims. They said that the police had to be divided willy-nilly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you think that that happened only in your municipality or do you think that that was at the level of all of Bosnia within the conference on Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I'm not aware of what was going on in the territory of all of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So there was an agreement and it was signed that there would be two municipalities and two public security stations; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But however, as far as I know, there was an ultimatum there, that that would happen willy-nilly, by hook or by crook.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you know that we accepted to have Bosnia leave Yugoslavia on those conditions and that that was a precondition? Do you know that; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 58 you say that there was a division, or rather, Rogatica complied with the requests of the Serbs to have a division of the municipality and in the police, but you say that the Serbs were not satisfied and were terrorising the people by putting up check-points - what was the word? - and so on and so forth. Are you saying that the Serbs gave up on the division or was it the Muslims who gave up on it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Well, as I have said, the division took place because that is what the Serbs wanted and they said that that would happen, willy-nilly, by hook or by crook.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who said that to you, Mr. Witness, that that is the way that it would be?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: No one said that to me, but these people who attended the negotiations then on the division of the police, they claimed that, and you can see who attended at the time, who the Bosniaks were who were working on this division with the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Over here you say that the Serbs started terrorising people and putting up check-points - what do we call them, check-points?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were the Serbs the first to put up check-points? You refer to April here. When did the first check-points appear?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I know that it was at the exit out of Rogatica. I used to go there towards Sarajevo. I heard that in the so-called Karanfil Mahala there was one check-point. As for these barricades, the first barricades were between the municipality building and the hotel. The Serbs blockaded that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that means that the Serb barricades came first?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Well, I meant barricades not check-points.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter number 07835. I believe it's actually been admitted already. I believe it has a P number. 07835 is the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is your recollection in terms of the date when any kind of barricades appeared, April or before that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I cannot remember. It's been quite a while. I cannot remember exactly. I cannot give you the exact date when this started. I know for sure that it was before the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Witness, please take a look at this. An agreement was reached to divide the municipality to have every local commune with the Muslim population conduct its own business within its own municipality and the Serbs in their own. The Serb policemen should keep law and order in Serb areas and Muslims in Muslim areas. And then on the 23rd of March, look at this first sentence, the Muslims are putting up barricades and the Serbs respond on the 24th. Look at the first three lines of this report sent to the BH Presidency.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you don't know who it was that put up roadblocks first, you think it was the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes, what I saw. I can speak about what I saw myself. I cannot talk about things that I have not seen myself. I know for sure that at this so-called Karanfil Mahala there were Serb check-points as you call them and there were checks carried out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has been admitted? It has a P number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P3271, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you talk about Karanfil Mahala and about people, Serbs, who were at those check-points conducting the checks. What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: They wore camouflage uniforms and SMB uniforms, olive-green-grey. I do not remember the insignia they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You then say in paragraph 3 of your statement -- actually, you talk about work, don't you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I beg your pardon. It's some different paragraph. Just a moment, please. Paragraph 9 on page 3, if it's still the same, I mean if the numbers are still the same. You say that because of the security situation that was becoming increasingly complex, the safety of the citizens was jeopardised, the management of the company where you worked decided in mid-April 1992 that you should go to work only once a week. You say that as far as you remember it was only on Mondays. Since you lived in the country, you went to work by bus; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Until when did you work?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I worked until the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But over here it says that in mid-April it was decided that you would only go to work once a week. How long did that go on?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Before I used to come in only on Mondays, but after the 15th of April I never came again. I never came again, other employees did, but I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I did not go because there were these check-points, as I said, and because these checks were carried out, these searches and I was afraid. I'm not sure exactly what the date was, but Batanovic, when he wanted to go around that roadblock, trying to avoid it, he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-ha. Why would that be a reason for them to arrest you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I don't know. There was no reason, but there was no reason for what I experienced and look at what happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, you said in your statement dated the 12th of January, 1994, paragraph 2, that in mid-April, because of these check-points, you and most Muslims decided not to go to work, right, for a while. That's what your statement says.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, as far as I know, the Romanija Corps passed through Rogatica -- actually, it was on the 14th of April. They passed through all their equipment and there was shooting in town. And on the next day people didn't go to work again. I personally did not go anymore. On the 14th of April I went to Rogatica for the last time and I never went again. I don't know whether other people came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that on the 15th of April the Romanija Corps did not exist?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I'm saying that I don't know which corps it was, but I do know that a large convoy passed through town, then they came from Kovan, I was in Rogatica at the time and they went in the direction of Mesici. Which corps it was exactly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So Kovan is farther away from the Serbian border and Mesici is closer to the Serbian border, so they passed through this part of Bosnia, going from the depth of Bosnia to the outskirts of Bosnia, right, towards Serbia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: I told you where they went and I don't know where they went after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, it would be a good thing if the Trial Chamber knew whether Kovan is closer to Serbia or is it Mesici that is closer to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-607
utterances.text: Well, Mesici is closer to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I note the time, so we'll adjourn for today and continue tomorrow morning. Sir, during the break -- we'll continue tomorrow, but during the break you are required not to discuss with anybody else about your testimony. I take it that you understand that? We'll start tomorrow at 10.00 and we'll sit until 3.30, as indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 7th day of September, 2011, at 10.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.59 p.m.,
